Subject: Redwood private endpoint - trust model and CSR process

Hi Aisha / Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier. We are trying to finalize the plan for connecting Redwood's runtime to our internal private endpoint for the FinCore sandbox environment. A few items we need to lock down from your side: 

- Does Redwood support using our internal CA chain (offline, air-gapped CA) as the trust anchor for service TLS to a private FQDN?
- If we provide a CSR signed by our CA, what format and SAN requirements do you need?
- We want to keep DNS split-horizon (external resolves to public proxy, internal resolves to private IP). Is there a recommended pattern for TTL, health checks, and failover if the private path becomes unreachable?
- We're interested in an "ephemeral TLS proxy" approach: a lightweight customer-managed proxy in our VPC that terminates customer TLS and uses a mutual TLS or token-based connection to Redwood. Any guidance on cert rotation and automated deployment?

We have some security constraints (SOC 2 scoping) so any dataflow diagrams or checklist you can share would help our auditors.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Director, InfraOps | FinCore

Subject: Re: Redwood private endpoint - trust model and CSR process

Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. High-level response and a proposed path forward below. I attached a short checklist for the ephemeral TLS proxy we generally share with customers.

Short answers:
1) Yes — we can trust a customer-managed CA for private endpoints. We validate the bundle you provide and install it on the dedicated runtime route that will serve your VPC. This requires the CA chain (PEM) and a signing process for the server certificate (CSR).
2) CSR/SAN requirements: include the fully-qualified internal hostname(s) you will use (e.g., api.private.fincore.internal). If you have a client cert requirement (mTLS) include the intended client identity OIDs. We prefer PEM-formatted CSR and will return a signed cert artifact and a small installation manifest.
3) Split-horizon DNS guidance: short TTLs (60-300s) plus active health checks. Our recommended pattern is: primary internal path -> customer-managed ephemeral TLS proxy (terminates customer certificate) -> private routing to Redwood peering. Secondary path -> Redwood public edge (fallback). We can automate fallback via DNS health checks that your DNS provider can perform.
4) Ephemeral TLS proxy pattern: customer deploys a small proxy (NLB + lightweight proxy, e.g., Envoy/nginx) that holds the customer cert. Proxy rotates certs via your automation (SSM/Ansible) and presents mutual TLS to Redwood or uses token-based client auth depending on your policy. We can accept either as long as the proxy authenticates to our runtime.

Next steps I propose:
- You send the CA bundle and an example CSR for us to validate format (we can do a dry-run).
- Karthik will provide an ops playbook with example configs and a minimal health-check/DNS recipe.
- Marissa will share the compliance checklist and a short Dataflow diagram for auditors.

I've attached: fincore-ephemeral-proxy-checklist.pdf (checklist + minimal network diagram).

Would a 30-minute sync on Tuesday to finalize cutover windows work?

—Aisha
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Sanjay / team,

Quick ops-level playbook to make the integration less hand-wavy. This is low-friction and used by a few other customers running split-horizon networks.

Pre-flight (customer):
- Generate CSR on your proxy host(s) with SANs: internal FQDN(s) and IP(s) if you insist. Example: CN=api.private.fincore.internal, SAN=DNS:api.private.fincore.internal,IP:10.10.5.12
- Provide CA chain in PEM, plus the cert signing function output (we only need the signed server cert later).

Proxy deployment options (pick one):
A) Terminates TLS on the proxy; proxy->Redwood uses mTLS (client cert) over private peering. Requires you to install a client cert issued by your CA and provide the client cert chain to Redwood.
B) Terminates TLS on proxy and establishes a short-lived HTTPS session to Redwood public edge using token-based auth. Simpler but has different audit surface.

DNS / failover recipe:
- Split-horizon authoritative zone for private clients -> records point to internal IPs behind the proxy. TTL 120s.
- Public authoritative zone -> records point to Redwood public edge. TTL 60s.
- Health check: probe proxy health from an external monitor (or Redwood's probe if you allow) and flip the public record to private when healthy. If private path fails, clients resolve to the public edge.

Cert rotation guidance:
- Short-lived server certs (30–90 days) preferred for ephemeral proxies. Use automated renewal; keep a signing endpoint that can be called by the proxy.
- We avoid using ACME for offline CAs. Instead: generate CSR on proxy -> you sign with offline CA -> upload signed cert to proxy via SSM/gitops job.

Minimal nginx example (proxy termination):
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  server_name api.private.fincore.internal;
  ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/certs/server.pem;
  ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/private/server.key;
  # mTLS to Redwood: upstream uses client cert if you choose option A
}

I'll prepare a one-page playbook with exact commands and a test checklist if you want to run a dry-run this week.

- Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
